When Anne Shirley and Diana Barry accidentally stumbled upon her home, Lavendar welcomed them warmly, finding in Anne a true kindred spirit. Through Anne, Lavendar met Stephen's son, Paul Irving, with whom she instantly formed a deep, maternal bond. Upon learning of her whereabouts from Paul, Stephen Irving returned to Prince Edward Island to seek out Lavendar. The two reconciled, rekindling their old affection, and were married in the garden at Echo Lodge in the late summer. Following their wedding, they embarked on a trip to the Pacific coast and subsequently settled in Boston, returning to spend their summers at Echo Lodge.

His teachers did not think him brilliant, but he was a good, all-round student. He never took things on faith; he always liked to investigate the truth of a statement for himself. Once Susan had told him that if he touched his tongue to a frosty latch all the skin would tear off it. Jem had promptly done it, “just to see if it was so.” He found it was “so,” at the cost of a very sore tongue for several days. But Jem did not grudge suffering in the interests of science. By constant experiment and observation he learned a great deal and his brothers and sisters thought his extensive knowledge of their little world quite wonderful. Jem always knew where the first and ripest berries grew, where the first pale violets shyly wakened from their winter’s sleep, and how many blue eggs were in a given robin’s nest in the maple grove. He could tell fortunes from daisy petals and suck honey from red clovers, and grub up all sorts of edible roots on the banks of the pond, while Susan went in daily fear that they would all be poisoned. unit: Leslie's early life in Four Winds was marked by tragedy: her beloved brother Kenneth was killed in a wagon accident, and two years later her despondent father hanged himself. To save her widowed mother from being evicted from their farm, sixteen-year-old Leslie agreed to marry Dick Moore, whom she did not love. Shortly after her mother's death, Dick sailed away on the Four Sisters and disappeared. Captain Jim later found an amnesiac man in Havana whom he believed to be Dick Moore and brought him back to Four Winds. For twelve years, Leslie faithfully cared for the brain-damaged man, living in poverty and isolation in her ancestral homestead. Upon the arrival of Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe at Four Winds, Leslie initially felt a bitter envy toward Anne's happiness. However, she eventually confessed her feelings to Anne, breaking down her emotional barriers, and the two became devoted friends. When Gilbert suggested an operation that might restore Dick's memory, Leslie courageously agreed despite her dread of returning to a life with the man she had once loathed. The operation in Montreal succeeded in restoring the man's memory, revealing that he was actually Dick's cousin, George Moore, and that the real Dick Moore had died years earlier in Cuba. Finally freed from her tragic burden, Leslie returned to Four Winds. She fell in love with Owen Ford, a writer who had stayed at her house during the summer while writing his novel based on Captain Jim's life-book. They confessed their mutual love in Anne's garden, and Owen proposed to her.
